prompt:
Find what the Node.js project officially says about the lifecycle of its LTS releases (how long Active LTS and Maintenance LTS last). Cite the official page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
According to the official Node.js project documentation, the support lifecycle for Long-Term Support (LTS) releases is defined by distinct phases with specific durations.

The following information is sourced directly from the official Node.js Release Working Group repository on GitHub, which is the authoritative source for release and support policies.

**Official Lifecycle Information:**

SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/Release | QUOTE: "Active LTS versions are supported for a year from the date an LTS version is announced, or until 6 months after the next LTS version is announced, whichever is longer." | CLAIM: Defines the duration of the Active LTS phase.
SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/Release | QUOTE: "Then, the version enters Maintenance mode for 18 months." | CLAIM: Defines the duration of the Maintenance LTS phase.
SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/Release | QUOTE: "All LTS releases receive a minimum of one year of active support and a total of 30 months of support starting from the LTS launch date." | CLAIM: Confirms the total support period (Active + Maintenance) is at least 30 months.

In summary, the official policy states that each LTS release goes through an Active LTS phase for a minimum of 12 months, followed by a Maintenance LTS phase for 18 months, resulting in a total support lifespan of 30 months. The exact transition from Active to Maintenance can be extended if the next LTS release is delayed.
